items.summary: Several women's organisations (AIDWA, NFIW, AIPWA, ALIFA) marched to Delhi Police headquarters Saturday over alleged sexual violence and police brutality against women during the anti-CEC/SIR protests. CPI leader Annie Raja told ANI the Centre is 'using sexual assault as a weapon' to silence women protesters, demanded action against the personnel involved and the resignation of Home Minister Amit Shah; she linked the march to the SIR-rollback and CEC-resignation demands, and noted Ankita Bhandari's parents joined. A parallel demonstration outside the HQ by SFI, AIMSS and KYS activists alleged police 'touching the women protestors' body parts inappropriately' (IANS). Delhi Police's counter: it slammed 'misleading social media claims' and said three women journalists' Oct-3 complaints were transferred to the Crime Branch for enquiry.
items.title: Women's groups march to Delhi Police HQ over alleged sexual violence at anti-CEC protests

items.summary: The planned 2 PM Press Club of India -> Jantar Mantar march is underway: two independent on-the-ground Instagram videos show demonstrators gathered outside the Press Club of India with 'RECLAIM JANTAR MANTAR' and 'GYANESH KUMAR MUST RESIGN' placards; one video (~2:30 PM) shows Delhi Police yellow barricades containing the crowd near the Press Club, speakers addressing protesters and media. A WatchDog TV reporter interviewed a protester demanding Jantar Mantar's reopening as a protest site and continued daily protests. A third small account's narration claims Neha Bora is leading the march - unverified.
items.title: 2 PM Press Club -> Jantar Mantar march materialises; protesters at Press Club of India
